title: studio: the CEL ConditionBuilder offers == / != on a list subject, and validateExpression accepts a condition that answers a constant
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by seat 4 area a4-D's dev on #35992 (os-dev report 7066498044).

## What happens
Studio's CEL `ConditionBuilder` offers `==` / `!=` when the subject is a list (a `multiple: true` field). The CEL engine then answers a constant: `record.labels == 'frontend'` is `false` for `['frontend','qa']`. `validateExpression` accepts the expression without a word, so the author saves a condition that can never match (or always matches with `!=`).

## Done when
On a list subject the builder offers membership (`in` / contains) instead of `==` / `!=`, or `validateExpression` refuses the comparison of a list with a scalar naming the field; a pin covers both the builder's operator list and the validator, with a scalar-field control.

reach: Studio form (an author's saved condition), measured once.
Business reason: conditions on multi-value fields silently never fire; the author has no signal.
Reader: a domain:ui lane (Studio condition builder) with the CEL validator owner.
Dedupe: `ConditionBuilder list ==` → 13 hits; open: #35992 only (the filter-condition builder that sends `=`/`$in`, a different builder and evaluator); the rest closed.
Grade: p2 — silent wrong behaviour at authoring time, no data loss.
